components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and lips, as in 吃, 喝, 吹; 吻 is a kiss.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for wěn; 物 wù shares the part.

example.hanzi: 母亲亲吻了孩子的额头。
example.pinyin: mǔqīn qīnwěnle háizi de étóu.
example.english: The mother kissed the child's forehead.
example.fact: Not all cultures practice romantic kissing. A 2015 cross-cultural survey found that fewer than half of the 168 societies studied showed any evidence of romantic-sexual kissing, suggesting it is a widespread but far from universal human custom rather than an innate behavior.

examples.hanzi: 她亲吻了一下小宝宝的脸。
examples.pinyin: Tā qīnwěn le yíxià xiǎo bǎobao de liǎn.
examples.english: She kissed the baby's face.

examples.hanzi: 电影的最后，他们在雨中亲吻。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng de zuìhòu, tāmen zài yǔ zhōng qīnwěn.
examples.english: At the end of the film, they kiss in the rain.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — hanging below the 口. Memory aid: a cloth dangling from a loop, so 'to hang' (吊灯 hanging lamp). The 'condole' sense (吊唁) is separate.
口 (mouth, opening) — the top. It may be only a loop or hook here; not a meaning clue. No settled etymology; treat the picture as a memory aid.

example.hanzi: 把灯吊在天花板上吧。
example.pinyin: Bǎ dēng diào zài tiānhuābǎn shàng ba.
example.english: Let's hang the lamp from the ceiling.
example.fact: 吊 gives many everyday words: 吊灯 (chandelier), 吊桥 (suspension bridge), 吊车 (crane), 吊带 (straps). In mainland slang, 吊 can also mean "awesome," as in 吊炸天. 吊唁 means to pay condolences.

examples.hanzi: 墙壁上吊着一幅画。
examples.pinyin: Qiángbì shang diào zhe yì fú huà.
examples.english: A painting hangs on the wall.

examples.hanzi: 起重机把货物吊到了楼上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐzhòngjī bǎ huòwù diào dào le lóu shang.
examples.english: The crane lifted the goods upstairs.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo strips, once written on, as in 笔, 等, 管: a slip, so simple and brief.
间 (jiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 这个方法很简单。
example.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ hěn jiǎndān.
example.english: This method is very simple.
example.fact: Before paper, Chinese was written on bamboo slips (竹简); short, narrow slips led to the sense of "brief" and "simple." You see it in 简单, 简历 (résumé), 简称 (abbreviation) and 简体字 (simplified characters).

examples.hanzi: 请用简单的话回答我。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng jiǎndān de huà huídá wǒ.
examples.english: Please answer me in simple words.

examples.hanzi: 这是我的简历。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de jiǎnlì.
examples.english: This is my résumé.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and gifts, as in 财, 货, 贵; 贡 is tribute presented.
工 (gōng) gives the sound: 贡 gòng is close, as in 功 gōng and 红 hóng.
犬 (dog) — a sacrifice was offered with a dog, hence 献 is to present or offer; the left side is a simplified stand-in.

example.hanzi: 他为公司的发展做出了巨大贡献。
example.pinyin: tā wèi gōngsī de fāzhǎn zuòchūle jùdà gòngxiàn.
example.english: He made a huge contribution to the company's development.
example.fact: Norman Borlaug, an agricultural scientist, is credited with contributions that saved an estimated one billion lives by breeding high-yield, disease-resistant wheat varieties during the mid-20th century "Green Revolution." He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for that work.

examples.hanzi: 每个人都应该为社会贡献自己的力量。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi wèi shèhuì gòngxiàn zìjǐ de lìliang.
examples.english: Everyone should contribute their strength to society.

examples.hanzi: 这位科学家的贡献得到了全世界的认可。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi kēxuéjiā de gòngxiàn dédào le quán shìjiè de rènkě.
examples.english: This scientist's contribution was recognized worldwide.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 她在公司里有很高的地位。
example.pinyin: tā zài gōngsī lǐ yǒu hěn gāo de dìwèi.
example.english: She holds a high status in the company.
example.fact: In naked mole-rat colonies, social status is enforced almost entirely by the queen, the colony's sole breeding female, who maintains her position partly through physical shoving of subordinates. Researchers have found her vertebrae actually lengthen after she takes power, letting her grow larger to reinforce her dominant status.

examples.hanzi: 现在女性的社会地位越来越高。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài nǚxìng de shèhuì dìwèi yuèláiyuè gāo.
examples.english: Women's social status is getting higher and higher now.

examples.hanzi: 中国在世界经济中占有重要地位。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó zài shìjiè jīngjì zhōng zhànyǒu zhòngyào dìwèi.
examples.english: China holds an important place in the world economy.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉旁) — marks jade and gems, as in 球, 珠, 玩; 琼 is fine jade.
京 (jīng) is only a loose sound hint for qióng.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 琼斯先生是我们的新老师。
example.pinyin: Qióngsī xiānsheng shì wǒmen de xīn lǎoshī.
example.english: Mr. Jones is our new teacher.
example.fact: "Jones" is one of the most common surnames in Wales, originating as a patronymic meaning "son of John." Because John was such a widespread given name in medieval Britain, Jones became disproportionately common in Welsh-speaking regions compared to the rest of the United Kingdom.

examples.hanzi: 琼斯太太每天早上都在花园里浇花。
examples.pinyin: Qióngsī tàitai měi tiān zǎoshang dōu zài huāyuán lǐ jiāohuā.
examples.english: Mrs. Jones waters the flowers in the garden every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我们的经理是琼斯先生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de jīnglǐ shì Qióngsī xiānsheng.
examples.english: Our manager is Mr. Jones.

meanings: to feel a twinge of guilt

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.
疒 (illness) — marks sickness and pain, as in 病, 痛, 疼; 疚 is the ache of guilt, as in 内疚.
久 (jiǔ) hints at the sound: 疚 jiù is close.

example.hanzi: 他因为说了谎而感到内疚。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi shuōle huǎng ér gǎndào nèijiù.
example.english: He felt guilty for having lied.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that feelings of guilt activate the same brain regions involved in physical pain processing, including the anterior insula. That is one reason researchers describe emotional guilt as genuinely "hurting" rather than being purely metaphorical.

examples.hanzi: 没能陪在妈妈身边，他心里很内疚。
examples.pinyin: Méi néng péi zài māma shēnbiān, tā xīnlǐ hěn nèijiù.
examples.english: He feels guilty about not being able to stay by his mother's side.

examples.hanzi: 你不用内疚，这不是你的错。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng nèijiù, zhè bú shì nǐ de cuò.
examples.english: You don't need to feel guilty; it's not your fault.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 这个系统运作得很稳定。
example.pinyin: zhège xìtǒng yùnzuò de hěn wěndìng.
example.english: This system operates very stably.
example.fact: The New York City subway operates around the clock, 24 hours a day, every day of the year, one of only a handful of major transit systems in the world that never fully shuts down for overnight maintenance. That forces crews to service tracks and trains while trains are still running on other lines.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的运作方式很特别。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de yùnzuò fāngshì hěn tèbié.
examples.english: This company's way of operating is very special.

examples.hanzi: 机器停了，整个工厂都无法运作。
examples.pinyin: Jīqì tíng le, zhěnggè gōngchǎng dōu wúfǎ yùnzuò.
examples.english: The machine stopped, and the whole factory can't operate.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 天气对比赛非常不利。
example.pinyin: tiānqì duì bǐsài fēicháng bùlì.
example.english: The weather is very unfavorable for the match.
example.fact: Home-field advantage in professional sports is measurable and real. Statisticians analyzing decades of soccer, basketball, and baseball results consistently find home teams win 55 to 60 percent of games, an edge researchers attribute to crowd noise affecting referee decisions as well as travel fatigue for the away side.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息对我们很不利。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi duì wǒmen hěn búlì.
examples.english: This news is very unfavorable for us.

examples.hanzi: 熬夜对身体健康不利。
examples.pinyin: Áoyè duì shēntǐ jiànkāng búlì.
examples.english: Staying up late is harmful to your health.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 潜水员潜入了海洋深处。
example.pinyin: qiánshuǐyuán qiánrùle hǎiyáng shēnchù.
example.english: The diver dove into the depths of the ocean.
example.fact: The deepest point in the ocean, the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, lies nearly 11,000 meters below the surface, deep enough that if Mount Everest were placed at its bottom, the peak would still sit over 2,000 meters underwater.

examples.hanzi: 他心灵深处一直藏着一个秘密。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīnlíng shēnchù yìzhí cángzhe yí gè mìmì.
examples.english: He has always hidden a secret deep in his heart.

examples.hanzi: 这条小路通向森林深处。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiǎolù tōng xiàng sēnlín shēnchù.
examples.english: This path leads deep into the forest.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks plants, as in 花, 草, 菜; 荡 is to sway or wash about.
汤 (tāng) stands in for the old part 昜 that also sounds out 场 chǎng, 扬 yáng and 烫 tàng.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妇 is a married woman.
彐 (hand) — 彐 is a hand holding a broom (the traditional 婦 had 帚), so a married woman who keeps house.

example.hanzi: 那部小说描写了一个被称为荡妇的女人。
example.pinyin: nà bù xiǎoshuō miáoxiěle yī gè bèi chēngwéi dàngfù de nǚrén.
example.english: That novel depicts a woman who is called a slut.
example.fact: The historical "scarlet letter" punishment in colonial New England, made famous by Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1850 novel, required women convicted of certain sexual offenses to visibly wear a mark identifying their status, a legal practice that existed in some Puritan colonies well before the novel dramatized it.

examples.hanzi: “荡妇”是一个带有侮辱性的词，不能随便用。
examples.pinyin: “Dàngfù” shì yí gè dàiyǒu wǔrǔxìng de cí, bù néng suíbiàn yòng.
examples.english: “Slut” is an insulting word and shouldn't be used casually.

examples.hanzi: 小说里的主人公被邻居们骂作荡妇。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshuō lǐ de zhǔréngōng bèi línjūmen mà zuò dàngfù.
examples.english: The heroine in the novel is called a slut by her neighbors.

components.note: 革 (leather) — marks hides, as in 鞋 shoe, 鞭 whip, 革命; 靴 is a boot.
化 (huà) is a loose hint for xuē; 花 huā and 货 huò share it.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 冬天穿这双靴子很暖和。
example.pinyin: dōngtiān chuān zhè shuāng xuēzi hěn nuǎnhuo.
example.english: Wearing these boots in winter is very warm.
example.fact: Cowboy boots developed their distinctive high heel not for fashion but for function. The raised heel keeps a rider's foot from sliding forward through the stirrup, an engineering solution that spread across cattle-ranching cultures in the American West during the 19th century.

examples.hanzi: 下雪天，我会穿一双厚靴子出门。
examples.pinyin: Xiàxuě tiān, wǒ huì chuān yì shuāng hòu xuēzi chūmén.
examples.english: On snowy days I wear a pair of thick boots out.

examples.hanzi: 这双靴子是皮的，很结实。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xuēzi shì pí de, hěn jiēshi.
examples.english: These boots are made of leather and are very sturdy.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 他找到了一个便宜的住处。
example.pinyin: tā zhǎodàole yī gè piányi de zhùchù.
example.english: He found a cheap residence.
example.fact: Cappadocia in central Turkey contains entire underground residences and even multi-story cities carved directly into soft volcanic rock starting more than a thousand years ago. The largest, Derinkuyu, could shelter up to 20,000 people along with their livestock and food stores during times of invasion.

examples.hanzi: 你的住处离公司远吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zhùchù lí gōngsī yuǎn ma?
examples.english: Is your place far from the company?

examples.hanzi: 他刚到这座城市，还没找到住处。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng dào zhè zuò chéngshì, hái méi zhǎodào zhùchù.
examples.english: He just arrived in this city and hasn't found a place to live yet.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister.
台 (tái) is a loose sound clue for shǐ; the same 台 gives 治 zhì and 怡 yí.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.

example.hanzi: 她始终相信自己能够成功。
example.pinyin: tā shǐzhōng xiāngxìn zìjǐ nénggòu chénggōng.
example.english: She always believed, from beginning to end, that she could succeed.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was not built as a single continuous project from beginning to end but assembled and extended piecemeal by different dynasties over roughly two thousand years. The best-preserved sections visible today date mainly from the Ming dynasty's rebuilding efforts in the 14th through 17th centuries.

examples.hanzi: 这几年，他始终没有放弃自己的梦想。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jǐ nián, tā shǐzhōng méiyǒu fàngqì zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: Over these years he has never given up his dream.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题始终没有解决。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí shǐzhōng méiyǒu jiějué.
examples.english: This problem has never been solved.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
车 (cart, vehicle) — marks wheeled things, as in 转, 轮, 较; 辆 counts vehicles.
两 (liǎng) hints at the sound: 辆 liàng is close.

example.hanzi: 这条路上的车辆非常多。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo lù shàng de chēliàng fēicháng duō.
example.english: There are a lot of vehicles on this road.
example.fact: Norway has the highest rate of electric vehicle adoption in the world, with battery-electric cars making up more than 90 percent of new vehicle sales by the mid-2020s, driven by heavy tax incentives and cheap hydroelectric power that keeps charging costs low.

examples.hanzi: 节假日高速公路上的车辆特别多。
examples.pinyin: Jiéjiàrì gāosù gōnglù shàng de chēliàng tèbié duō.
examples.english: There are especially many vehicles on the highway during holidays.

examples.hanzi: 这条路禁止大型车辆通行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù jìnzhǐ dàxíng chēliàng tōngxíng.
examples.english: Large vehicles are prohibited on this road.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸭 duck, 鹅 goose, 鸽 pigeon; 鸡 is a chicken. 又 only replaces the old sound part.

example.hanzi: 感恩节的时候人们会吃火鸡。
example.pinyin: gǎn'ēnjié de shíhou rénmen huì chī huǒjī.
example.english: People eat turkey during Thanksgiving.
example.fact: Despite its English name, the turkey bird has no biological connection to the country Turkey. It's a North American species domesticated by indigenous peoples in Mexico, and it picked up its confusing name in Europe because traders initially confused it with African guinea fowl imported through Turkish territory.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈烤了一只很大的火鸡。
examples.pinyin: Māma kǎo le yì zhī hěn dà de huǒjī.
examples.english: Mom roasted a very large turkey.

examples.hanzi: 农场里养着几只火鸡。
examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǎngzhe jǐ zhī huǒjī.
examples.english: There are a few turkeys raised on the farm.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 我经常和外国客户打交道。
example.pinyin: wǒ jīngcháng hé wàiguó kèhù dǎjiāodào.
example.english: I often have dealings with foreign clients.
example.fact: Diplomats posted abroad receive extensive briefings on local customs before having any official dealings with foreign governments, a practice formalized by the U.S. Foreign Service Institute's "area studies" training program established in the 1940s, which remains a model for diplomatic training worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 他不太会和陌生人打交道。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú tài huì hé mòshēngrén dǎjiāodao.
examples.english: He isn't good at dealing with strangers.

examples.hanzi: 做销售就要天天和客户打交道。
examples.pinyin: Zuò xiāoshòu jiù yào tiāntiān hé kèhù dǎjiāodao.
examples.english: In sales you have to deal with customers every day.

components.note: 几 (small table) — a low table with legs. As a sound it gives jī to 机 and 肌, and means how many in 几个.
白 (bái) hints at the sound: 百 bǎi is close, and 白 also gives 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.hanzi: 这次活动来了几百人。
example.pinyin: zhè cì huódòng láile jǐ bǎi rén.
example.english: Several hundred people came to this event.
example.fact: A group of starlings performing their famous swirling "murmuration" can number in the several hundred to several thousand birds. Physicists studying the phenomenon found each bird tracks only its seven nearest neighbors, a simple local rule that produces the mesmerizing, coordinated motion of the whole flock.

examples.hanzi: 这本书有几百页，要看很久。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu jǐbǎi yè, yào kàn hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: This book has several hundred pages and takes a long time to read.

examples.hanzi: 从这里到机场要几百块钱的车费。
examples.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào jīchǎng yào jǐbǎi kuài qián de chēfèi.
examples.english: A ride from here to the airport costs a few hundred yuan.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 他对这件事过于担心了。
example.pinyin: tā duì zhè jiàn shì guòyú dānxīnle.
example.english: He is excessively worried about this matter.
example.fact: The Yerkes-Dodson law, first proposed by psychologists in 1908, describes how performance improves with stress and arousal only up to a point. Beyond that point, excessive stress actually degrades performance, a curve now widely cited in sports psychology and workplace research.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划过于复杂，很难实现。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà guòyú fùzá, hěn nán shíxiàn.
examples.english: This plan is too complicated and hard to carry out.

examples.hanzi: 你不要过于自信。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyào guòyú zìxìn.
examples.english: Don't be overconfident.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech and breath, as in 吃, 叫, 喝; 呵 is a laugh or a breath out.
可 (kě) hints at the sound: 呵 hē is close, and 可 also gives 河 hé, 歌 gē and 何 hé.

example.hanzi: 他呵了一口气，暖了暖手。
example.pinyin: Tā hē le yì kǒu qì, nuǎnle nuǎn shǒu.
example.english: He breathed on his hands to warm them.
example.fact: 呵 literally means to puff out warm breath (呵气) and to scold (呵斥). It also gives 呵护 (to cherish and protect) and the laugh 呵呵, which in chats can sound curt or even sarcastic. A neutral particle reading ā/a also exists.

examples.hanzi: 呵呵,你说得对!
examples.pinyin: Hēhē, nǐ shuō de duì!
examples.english: Ha ha, you're right!

examples.hanzi: 冬天早上,人呵出的气是白色的。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān zǎoshang, rén hē chū de qì shì báisè de.
examples.english: On winter mornings, the breath people exhale looks white.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and speech, as in 吃, 喝, 吹; 唇 is the lip.
辰 (chén) hints at the sound: 唇 chún is close to 晨 chén and 振 zhèn.

example.hanzi: 她的嘴唇很干，要涂润唇膏。
example.pinyin: Tā de zuǐchún hěn gān, yào tú rùnchúngāo.
example.english: Her lips are dry, so she needs lip balm.
example.fact: On its own 唇 is mostly bound; people say 嘴唇 for lip. Related words are 唇膏 (lipstick) and the idiom 唇亡齿寒, "if the lips are gone, the teeth get cold," about neighbours whose fates are linked.

examples.hanzi: 她涂了红色的唇膏。
examples.pinyin: Tā tú le hóngsè de chúngāo.
examples.english: She put on red lipstick.

examples.hanzi: 他的嘴唇被风吹裂了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zuǐchún bèi fēng chuī liè le.
examples.english: His lips were chapped by the wind.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
女 (woman) — marks women and girls, as in 妈, 姐, 好; 妮 is a young girl, often in names.
尼 (ní) gives the sound: 妮 nī is close, as in 泥 ní.

example.hanzi: 安妮明天要去北京旅行。
example.pinyin: Ānní míngtiān yào qù Běijīng lǚxíng.
example.english: Annie is going to travel to Beijing tomorrow.
example.fact: The name Annie is a diminutive of Anne, ultimately derived from the Hebrew name Hannah, meaning "grace" or "favor." The same root lies behind names like Anna, Ann, and Nancy, which all trace back to the biblical figure Hannah in the Book of Samuel.

examples.hanzi: 安妮是我的英语老师。
examples.pinyin: Ānnī shì wǒ de Yīngyǔ lǎoshī.
examples.english: Annie is my English teacher.

examples.hanzi: 安妮和我是邻居，我们经常一起散步。
examples.pinyin: Ānnī hé wǒ shì línjū, wǒmen jīngcháng yìqǐ sànbù.
examples.english: Annie and I are neighbors and often walk together.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 账 is an account or bill.
长 (zhǎng) hints at the sound: 账 zhàng is close to 胀 zhàng and 帐 zhàng.
户 (door, household) — one half of a double door 門. As a radical it marks doors and rooms: 房 room, 所 place, 扇 fan.

example.hanzi: 请检查一下你的银行账户。
example.pinyin: qǐng jiǎnchá yīxià nǐ de yínháng zhànghù.
example.english: Please check your bank account.
example.fact: The world's first ATM was installed outside a Barclays branch in Enfield, London, in 1967, dispensing cash to account holders who inserted a paper voucher rather than the plastic card used today. The voucher was radioactively marked so the machine could detect it, a security measure quickly abandoned for safety reasons.

examples.hanzi: 你的账户里还有多少钱？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zhànghù lǐ hái yǒu duōshao qián?
examples.english: How much money is left in your account?

examples.hanzi: 我忘了社交媒体账户的密码。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàng le shèjiāo méitǐ zhànghù de mìmǎ.
examples.english: I forgot the password of my social media account.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.hanzi: 这张图像的分辨率很高。
example.pinyin: zhè zhāng túxiàng de fēnbiànlǜ hěn gāo.
example.english: This image has a very high resolution.
example.fact: The first digital image ever scanned was a photograph of Russell Kirsch's infant son in 1957, captured at a resolution of just 176 by 176 pixels using a rotating drum scanner Kirsch built at the U.S. National Bureau of Standards, a milestone considered the birth of digital imaging.

examples.hanzi: 这张照片的图像有点模糊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn de túxiàng yǒudiǎn móhu.
examples.english: The image in this photo is a bit blurry.

examples.hanzi: 医生通过图像检查他的内脏。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng tōngguò túxiàng jiǎnchá tā de nèizàng.
examples.english: The doctor examined his organs through imaging.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 撒 is scattering or letting go.
散 (sàn) scatter is the meaning-sound part: a hand 扌 scattering, with sā/sàn close in sound.
一 (horizon) — the sun 日 just rising above the ground line: dawn. 旦 also sounds out 担 dān, 但 dàn and 胆 dǎn.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了一个关于撒旦的故事。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle yī gè guānyú Sādàn de gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells a story about Satan.
example.fact: The name "Satan" derives from a Hebrew word meaning "adversary" or "accuser," and in the earliest Hebrew scriptures it functioned more as a role or title, an accusing prosecutor figure in a heavenly court, rather than the singular personified embodiment of evil that later Christian theology developed.

examples.hanzi: 在这个故事里，撒旦是邪恶的象征。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhège gùshi lǐ, Sādàn shì xié'è de xiàngzhēng.
examples.english: In this story, Satan is a symbol of evil.

examples.hanzi: 这首诗把战争比作撒旦的杰作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu shī bǎ zhànzhēng bǐ zuò Sādàn de jiézuò.
examples.english: This poem likens war to the masterpiece of Satan.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了他的同伙。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng dàibǔle tā de tónghuǒ.
example.english: The police arrested his accomplice.
example.fact: Wolves hunting in packs coordinate with their fellow pack members using specific howl patterns that researchers have shown convey information about the group's location and readiness to hunt, effectively letting accomplices synchronize an ambush across long distances in dense terrain.

examples.hanzi: 小偷的同伙在外面放风。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu de tónghuǒ zài wàimiàn fàngfēng.
examples.english: The thief's accomplice kept watch outside.

examples.hanzi: 他不肯说出同伙的名字。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù kěn shuō chū tónghuǒ de míngzi.
examples.english: He refused to give the name of his accomplice.

components.note: 阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — hills, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sunny side; 隆 is high and grand.

example.hanzi: 今天的会议很隆重。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de huìyì hěn lóngzhòng.
example.english: Today's meeting is very grand.
example.fact: 隆 means high, grand or flourishing: 隆重 (solemn and grand), 隆冬 (the depths of winter), 隆起 (to bulge). It also appears in 乾隆, the Qianlong emperor's era name, and in 轰隆, a rumbling sound.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的生意很兴隆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de shēngyi hěn xīnglóng.
examples.english: This restaurant's business is booming.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着隆重的西装去参加婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe lóngzhòng de xīzhuāng qù cānjiā hūnlǐ.
examples.english: He wore a formal suit to the wedding.

components.note: 井 (well) — a picture of a well frame, a square curb around a shaft, as in 水井 water well.

example.hanzi: 村子里有一口老井。
example.pinyin: Cūnzi lǐ yǒu yì kǒu lǎo jǐng.
example.english: There is an old well in the village.
example.fact: The measure word for wells is 口: 一口井. 井 also appears in 水井 (water well), 油井 (oil well), 天井 (courtyard), and the idiom 井井有条 (in perfect order). Because of its shape, 井 is the Chinese name for the # symbol.

examples.hanzi: 他从水井里打了一桶水。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng shuǐjǐng li dǎ le yì tǒng shuǐ.
examples.english: He drew a bucket of water from the well.

examples.hanzi: 那座山上有一口古井。
examples.pinyin: Nà zuò shān shang yǒu yì kǒu gǔjǐng.
examples.english: There is an ancient well on that mountain.

components.note: 死 (dead) — 毙 is dying or killing, as in 枪毙 shoot dead.
比 (bǐ) — loose sound hint (bì vs bǐ).

example.hanzi: 警察当场把那个坏人击毙了。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá dāngchǎng bǎ nàge huàirén jībì le.
example.english: The police shot the criminal dead on the spot.
example.fact: 毙 appears in 击毙 and 枪毙 (to shoot dead). In office talk it has a colloquial sense, "to reject": 方案被毙了 means "the proposal got shot down," borrowing the violent image.

examples.hanzi: 那只野猪被猎人击毙了。
examples.pinyin: Nà zhī yězhū bèi lièrén jībì le.
examples.english: The wild boar was shot dead by the hunter.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划被老板毙掉了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà bèi lǎobǎn bì diào le.
examples.english: This plan was vetoed by the boss.

components.note: 至 (zhì) — same sound — 致 is zhì, like 至 (to arrive); 致 is to cause to arrive, then to bring about.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action performed, as in 教, 放, 收.

example.hanzi: 大雨导致了严重的堵车。
example.pinyin: Dàyǔ dǎozhì le yánzhòng de dǔchē.
example.english: The heavy rain caused a serious traffic jam.
example.fact: 导致 usually introduces a bad outcome, unlike neutral 引起 or positive 促成. 致 itself conveys messages: 致谢, 致电, 致辞 (give a speech), and letters close with 此致敬礼. Also 致富 (to get rich) and 一致 (in agreement).

examples.hanzi: 我要向你致谢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào xiàng nǐ zhìxiè.
examples.english: I want to thank you.

examples.hanzi: 他们的看法一致。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de kànfǎ yízhì.
examples.english: Their views are the same.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 听到消息后，他立刻赶来了。
example.pinyin: tīngdào xiāoxi hòu, tā lìkè gǎnláile.
example.english: After hearing the news, he rushed over immediately.
example.fact: Emergency medical responders rushing to a cardiac arrest are trained around what's sometimes called the "golden ten minutes": brain damage from oxygen deprivation begins within about four to six minutes, which is why bystander CPR performed before paramedics arrive dramatically improves survival odds.

examples.hanzi: 消防车很快就赶来了。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángchē hěn kuài jiù gǎnlái le.
examples.english: The fire truck rushed over very soon.

examples.hanzi: 他从外地赶来参加我的婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng wàidì gǎnlái cānjiā wǒ de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: He rushed in from another city to attend my wedding.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 腿 leg, 脚 foot, 肚 belly; 股 is the thigh or rump, later a share.
殳 (shū, weapon in hand) — only a loose sound hint; it also appears in 投 and 设.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 他昨天买了一些股票。
example.pinyin: tā zuótiān mǎile yīxiē gǔpiào.
example.english: He bought some stocks yesterday.
example.fact: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, issued the world's first publicly tradable stock, and its shares were bought and sold on what became the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, arguably the birthplace of the modern stock market, more than a century before the London or New York exchanges existed.

examples.hanzi: 他把大部分钱都投到了股票里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ dàbùfen qián dōu tóu dào le gǔpiào lǐ.
examples.english: He put most of his money into stocks.

examples.hanzi: 今天这只股票的价格下跌了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zhè zhī gǔpiào de jiàgé xiàdiē le.
examples.english: The price of this stock fell today.

components.note: 丰 — a picture of lush growing grain or grass: plenty, as in 丰富.
宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; 富 is a house full of goods, hence rich.
畐 (fú) gives the sound: 富 fù is close, as in 福 fú and 副 fù.

example.hanzi: 这个地区的自然资源非常丰富。
example.pinyin: zhège dìqū de zìrán zīyuán fēicháng fēngfù.
example.english: This region's natural resources are very abundant.
example.fact: The Democratic Republic of the Congo holds some of the most abundant mineral reserves on Earth, including over half the world's known cobalt supply, an element now critical to manufacturing the lithium-ion batteries used in smartphones and electric vehicles.

examples.hanzi: 他的人生经历非常丰富。
examples.pinyin: Tā de rénshēng jīnglì fēicháng fēngfù.
examples.english: His life experience is very rich.

examples.hanzi: 学校想办法丰富学生的课余生活。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xiǎng bànfǎ fēngfù xuésheng de kèyú shēnghuó.
examples.english: The school is finding ways to enrich students' after-class life.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 插 is to stick in.
臿 (chā) gives the sound exactly: 插 chā.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 别插手别人的私事。
example.pinyin: bié chāshǒu biérén de sīshì.
example.english: Don't meddle in other people's private affairs.
example.fact: The Prime Directive in the fictional "Star Trek" universe, a rule barring interference in the natural development of other civilizations, was directly inspired by real anthropological debates in the 1960s about whether contact with isolated human societies does more harm than good, a concern still actively discussed by anthropologists studying uncontacted peoples today.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们家的事，你别插手。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen jiā de shì, nǐ bié chāshǒu.
examples.english: This is our family's business; don't get involved.

examples.hanzi: 老板不想插手员工之间的小矛盾。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn bù xiǎng chāshǒu yuángōng zhījiān de xiǎo máodùn.
examples.english: The boss doesn't want to meddle in small conflicts among employees.

meanings: (Tw) to interview (e.g. for a report or feature story)

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说, 语, 请; 访 is to visit and ask.
方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 访 fǎng is close, as in 仿 fǎng and 纺 fǎng.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 科学家们访问了南极的科考站。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiāmen fǎngwèn le Nánjí de kēkǎozhàn.
example.english: The scientists visited the research station in Antarctica.
example.fact: Antarctica's McMurdo Station, the continent's largest research base, houses around 1,000 people in summer but fewer than 200 through the dark winter months — its buildings sit on volcanic rock near Mount Erebus, one of the few permanently active volcanoes on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 总统下个月将访问中国。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng xià gè yuè jiāng fǎngwèn Zhōngguó.
examples.english: The president will visit China next month.

examples.hanzi: 这个网站每天有上万人访问。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wǎngzhàn měi tiān yǒu shàng wàn rén fǎngwèn.
examples.english: This website is visited by tens of thousands of people every day.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 探险队设法穿过了茂密的雨林。
example.pinyin: tànxiǎnduì shèfǎ chuānguò le màomì de yǔlín.
example.english: The expedition team found a way to cross the dense rainforest.
example.fact: The Amazon rainforest produces roughly 20% of the world's oxygen and is home to an estimated 10% of all known species on Earth. Satellite monitoring shows it has lost about 17% of its original forest cover since 1970 to logging and agriculture.

examples.hanzi: 我会设法按时完成这份报告。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì shèfǎ ànshí wánchéng zhè fèn bàogào.
examples.english: I'll try to finish this report on time.

examples.hanzi: 他设法联系上了失散多年的哥哥。
examples.pinyin: Tā shèfǎ liánxì shàng le shīsàn duō nián de gēge.
examples.english: He managed to get in touch with his long-lost brother.

meanings: interjection of wonder, shock or admiration

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech and exclamations, as in 啊, 呀, 哦; 哎 is a cry of surprise.
艾 (ài) hints at the sound: 哎 āi is close.
口 (mouth) — marks speech and exclamations, as in 啊, 哎, 哦; 呀 is a soft particle.
牙 (yá) hints at the sound: 呀 ya is close to 芽 yá and 鸦 yā.

example.hanzi: 哎呀,火山突然喷发了!
example.pinyin: āiyā, huǒshān tūrán pēnfā le!
example.english: Oh no, the volcano suddenly erupted!
example.fact: When Krakatoa erupted in 1883, the explosion was so loud it ruptured eardrums of sailors 40 miles away and was heard clearly nearly 3,000 miles away in Australia — one of the loudest sounds ever recorded in human history.

examples.hanzi: 哎呀，我忘了带钥匙！
examples.pinyin: Āiyā, wǒ wàng le dài yàoshi!
examples.english: Oh no, I forgot my keys!

examples.hanzi: 哎呀，你今天这身衣服真好看！
examples.pinyin: Āiyā, nǐ jīntiān zhè shēn yīfu zhēn hǎokàn!
examples.english: Wow, you look great in that outfit today!

components.note: 忄 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 情, 快, 怕; 慷 is generous feeling (慷慨).
康 (kāng) gives the sound exactly: 慷 kāng.
忄 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 情, 快, 怕; 慨 is a sigh or stirring of feeling (慷慨).
既 (jì) is a loose hint for kǎi; 概 gài and 溉 gài share it.

example.hanzi: 那位商人慷慨地捐赠了一座图书馆。
example.pinyin: nà wèi shāngrén kāngkǎi de juānzèng le yí zuò túshūguǎn.
example.english: That merchant generously donated a library.
example.fact: Andrew Carnegie gave away roughly 90% of his fortune during his lifetime, funding over 2,500 public libraries around the world. It remains a philanthropic model still studied today for spreading free access to knowledge across small towns.

examples.hanzi: 他对朋友一向很慷慨。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou yíxiàng hěn kāngkǎi.
examples.english: He has always been generous to his friends.

examples.hanzi: 校长慷慨激昂地发表了演讲。
examples.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng kāngkǎi jī'áng de fābiǎo le yǎnjiǎng.
examples.english: The principal gave an impassioned speech.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.
夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.

example.hanzi: 登山者在浓雾中迷失了方向。
example.pinyin: dēngshānzhě zài nóngwù zhōng míshī le fāngxiàng.
example.english: The climber lost his sense of direction in the thick fog.
example.fact: Magnetic north drifts constantly — it has moved over 600 miles across the Arctic since 1900 and is currently migrating toward Siberia at roughly 30 miles per year, forcing periodic updates to navigation charts and compass calibrations worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 在大城市里，很多年轻人迷失了自己。
examples.pinyin: Zài dà chéngshì lǐ, hěn duō niánqīngrén míshī le zìjǐ.
examples.english: In big cities, many young people lose themselves.

examples.hanzi: 小孩在人群中迷失了方向。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái zài rénqún zhōng míshī le fāngxiàng.
examples.english: The child lost his way in the crowd.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸; thread is the classic fine thing, so 细 means thin, slender, then detailed — as in 线 line, 红 red.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胞 is the womb, then a cell (细胞).
包 (bāo) gives the sound exactly: 胞 bāo, also in 饱 bǎo and 抱 bào.

example.hanzi: 显微镜下可以看到细胞的结构。
example.pinyin: xiǎnwéijìng xià kěyǐ kàndào xìbāo de jiégòu.
example.english: Under the microscope you can see the structure of the cell.
example.fact: The human body contains an estimated 37 trillion cells, and red blood cells alone are replaced at a rate of about 2 million per second. That means nearly the entire population of red blood cells turns over roughly every four months.

examples.hanzi: 人体由几十万亿个细胞组成。
examples.pinyin: Réntǐ yóu jǐ shí wàn yì gè xìbāo zǔchéng.
examples.english: The human body is made up of tens of trillions of cells.

examples.hanzi: 这种药可以杀死癌细胞。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào kěyǐ shāsǐ ái xìbāo.
examples.english: This medicine can kill cancer cells.

components.note: 马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.
尸 (body) — originally a person seated or lying; as a radical it is in 尾 tail, 层 floor, 居 reside, 屋 house.

example.hanzi: 法医对尸体进行了验尸。
example.pinyin: fǎyī duì shītǐ jìnxíng le yànshī.
example.english: The forensic examiner performed an autopsy on the body.
example.fact: The word "autopsy" comes from the Greek "autopsia," meaning "to see for oneself." The practice dates back to ancient Alexandria, where physicians such as Herophilus conducted systematic human dissections around 300 BC to study anatomy.

examples.hanzi: 验尸报告明天才能出来。
examples.pinyin: Yànshī bàogào míngtiān cái néng chūlái.
examples.english: The autopsy report won't be out until tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 警察要求对死者进行验尸。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yāoqiú duì sǐzhě jìnxíng yànshī.
examples.english: The police asked for an autopsy to be performed on the deceased.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.

example.hanzi: 他每晚都在阳台上看星星。
example.pinyin: tā měiwǎn dōu zài yángtái shàng kàn xīngxīng.
example.english: Every night he watches the stars from the balcony.
example.fact: Light pollution now hides the Milky Way from more than a third of humanity, including nearly 80% of North Americans. That's a remarkably recent change — as late as the 1950s, most of the world's population could still see it clearly from their backyard.

examples.hanzi: 我每晚十一点睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi wǎn shíyī diǎn shuìjiào.
examples.english: I go to bed at eleven every night.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们每晚都要听一个故事才肯睡。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen měi wǎn dōu yào tīng yí gè gùshi cái kěn shuì.
examples.english: The kids won't sleep unless they hear a story every night.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 押 is holding something as security or in custody, as in 押金 deposit.
甲 (jiǎ) — loose sound hint (yā vs jiǎ).

example.hanzi: 警察把小偷押走了。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ xiǎotōu yā zǒu le.
example.english: The police took the thief away in custody.
example.fact: 押 covers both holding people (押送, to escort) and putting up security. 押金 is the deposit you pay when renting an apartment or bike; rentals are often described as 押一付三. 押韵 (yā yùn) means to rhyme.

examples.hanzi: 警察把犯人押上了车。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ fànrén yā shàng le chē.
examples.english: The police escorted the suspect onto the vehicle.

examples.hanzi: 请把你的身份证押在这里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de shēnfènzhèng yā zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: Please leave your ID here as a deposit.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 长期的风化作用形成了这片沙漠。
example.pinyin: chángqī de fēnghuà zuòyòng xíngchéng le zhè piàn shāmò.
example.english: Long-term weathering formed this desert.
example.fact: The Sahara has actually flipped between desert and lush grassland roughly every 20,000 years due to shifts in Earth's axial tilt, a cycle called the "green Sahara" period. The most recent green phase ended only about 5,000 years ago.

examples.hanzi: 早起慢慢形成了他的习惯。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoqǐ mànmàn xíngchéng le tā de xíguàn.
examples.english: Getting up early gradually became his habit.

examples.hanzi: 云是由小水滴形成的。
examples.pinyin: Yún shì yóu xiǎo shuǐdī xíngchéng de.
examples.english: Clouds are formed from tiny water droplets.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
临 (simplified 臨) — the old form shows a person bending over with a watching eye above a heap of goods: looking down on something, hence 'to face, to draw near'.

example.hanzi: 冬天的来临让北极熊开始寻找食物。
example.pinyin: dōngtiān de láilín ràng běijíxióng kāishǐ xúnzhǎo shíwù.
example.english: The arrival of winter prompts polar bears to start searching for food.
example.fact: Polar bears can smell a seal's breathing hole through nearly three feet of compacted snow and ice. Their stomachs can stretch to hold up to 150 pounds of food after a successful hunt, critical for surviving months of sparse hunting.

examples.hanzi: 新年即将来临，大家都很期待。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián jíjiāng láilín, dàjiā dōu hěn qīdài.
examples.english: The New Year is about to arrive and everyone is looking forward to it.

examples.hanzi: 夜幕来临，街上亮起了灯。
examples.pinyin: Yèmù láilín, jiē shàng liàng qǐ le dēng.
examples.english: As night fell, lights came on in the street.

components.note: 子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.

example.hanzi: 双方终于了结了这场官司。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng zhōngyú liǎojié le zhè chǎng guānsi.
example.english: Both sides finally settled the lawsuit.
example.fact: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648, which finally settled the Thirty Years' War, involved simultaneous negotiations at two German cities, Münster and Osnabrück, because the warring Catholic and Protestant delegates refused to meet under the same roof. It remains one of the earliest examples of modern multilateral diplomacy.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我想尽快了结。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ xiǎng jǐnkuài liǎojié.
examples.english: I want to settle this matter as soon as possible.

examples.hanzi: 他终于了结了多年的心愿。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú liǎojié le duō nián de xīnyuàn.
examples.english: He finally fulfilled a wish he'd had for many years.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 人工智能正在改变许多行业。
example.pinyin: réngōng zhìnéng zhèngzài gǎibiàn xǔduō hángyè.
example.english: Artificial intelligence is transforming many industries.
example.fact: The global semiconductor industry produces over a trillion chips a year, yet more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips are manufactured by a single company, TSMC, in Taiwan. That concentration makes the industry unusually vulnerable to regional disruption.

examples.hanzi: 你在哪个行业工作？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài nǎge hángyè gōngzuò?
examples.english: What industry do you work in?

examples.hanzi: 这个行业的竞争非常激烈。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hángyè de jìngzhēng fēicháng jīliè.
examples.english: Competition in this industry is fierce.

meanings: abbr. for Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and herbs, as in 花, 草, 茶; 苏 originally named the perilla plant, and is also short for Jiangsu and Soviet (苏联).
耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.

example.hanzi: 1991年苏联解体了。
example.pinyin: 1991 nián Sūlián jiětǐ le.
example.english: The Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
example.fact: At its peak the Soviet Union spanned 11 time zones and covered roughly one-sixth of Earth's land surface. After its 1991 collapse, it split into fifteen independent countries, the largest peaceful dissolution of a state in modern history.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷年轻的时候去过苏联。
examples.pinyin: Yéye niánqīng de shíhou qù guo Sūlián.
examples.english: Grandpa went to the Soviet Union when he was young.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家出生在苏联时期。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā chūshēng zài Sūlián shíqī.
examples.english: This writer was born during the Soviet era.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 游; 潜 is to dive under the water, hence hidden, as in 潜水.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这个年轻球员展现出巨大的潜力。
example.pinyin: zhège niánqīng qiúyuán zhǎnxiàn chū jùdà de qiánlì.
example.english: This young player has shown enormous potential.
example.fact: The human brain uses about 20% of the body's total energy despite making up just 2% of body weight. The popular myth that people use "only 10% of their brain," however, is false — imaging shows nearly all brain regions are active over a typical day.

examples.hanzi: 每个孩子都有自己的潜力。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè háizi dōu yǒu zìjǐ de qiánlì.
examples.english: Every child has his or her own potential.

examples.hanzi: 这个市场很有潜力。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shìchǎng hěn yǒu qiánlì.
examples.english: This market has great potential.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks rivers and water, as in 河, 海, 江; 汉 is the Han River, which gave name to the Han dynasty and people.

example.hanzi: 他是汉族人，会说汉语。
example.pinyin: Tā shì Hànzú rén, huì shuō Hànyǔ.
example.english: He is Han Chinese and speaks Chinese.
example.fact: 汉 comes from the Han dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), which gave the Chinese majority its name: 汉族, 汉语 (Chinese language), 汉字 (characters). It also means a man in 好汉 (a brave fellow) and 男子汉 (a real man).

examples.hanzi: 他是一个好汉。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hǎohàn.
examples.english: He is a real man of courage.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一本汉字字典。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì běn Hànzì zìdiǎn.
examples.english: I want to buy a Chinese character dictionary.
